title: Loaded Game Day Nachos
seoTitle: Loaded Game Day Nachos | Firefighter Meal
shortDescription: Chip mountain for the whole couch
subtitle: Chip mountain for the whole couch
description: Chip mountain for the whole couch. Sized for a full crew, with timing that still works when the kitchen gets interrupted.
equipment: Large cast iron skillet or Dutch oven

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Loaded Game Day Nachos in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on. Use Pickled jalapeños, sliced as listed — measure each before heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch beef. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Brown the beef
steps.instruction: Brown ground beef in a large skillet over medium-high, breaking it into fine crumbles. Drain excess grease — wet beef makes soggy chips. Stir in taco seasoning and ½ cup water; simmer 5 minutes until saucy. Target 145°F for steaks, 160°F for ground at the thickest point before moving to the next batch.

steps.title: Build chip trays
steps.instruction: Spread chips in a single layer on two full-size sheet pans — double layers steam instead of crisp. Scatter half the cheese over chips.

steps.title: Melt and load
steps.instruction: Broil at 450°F 3–4 minutes until cheese bubbles at the edges. Pull pans, add seasoned beef, remaining cheese, and jalapeños. Broil 2 more minutes until cheese is fully melted. Target 145°F for steaks, 160°F for ground at the thickest point before moving to the next batch.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 145°F for medium beef, 160°F for ground. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-service, cover finished food and hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven — never leave proteins below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Note the hold time on the pan with a grease pencil.

steps.title: Portion and open the line
steps.instruction: Portion Loaded Game Day Nachos onto sheet trays or hotel pans for family-style service. Stack plates, forks, and napkins at the end of the line so late-arriving crew can self-serve without bottlenecking the cook.

steps.title: Scale for larger halls
steps.instruction: When cooking for more than 8 firefighters, split into two pans halfway through so the bottom layer does not overcook while the top waits — duplicate mise en place if you double batches.

steps.title: Serve immediately
steps.instruction: Top with pico and sour cream at the table — not before, or chips wilt. Loaded Game Day Nachos die fast; make a second tray when the first is half gone.

steps.title: Final quality check before service
steps.instruction: Walk the line once before opening service for Loaded Game Day Nachos — confirm hotel pans are labeled, backup trays are in the 200°F oven, and thermometers are calibrated. Rookies should ask a senior cook to spot-check the first portion.

proTips: Keep a backup tray warm in the oven for late calls — nothing worse than cold plates after a run.
Taste for salt at the end — hall palates run salty after long shifts.
tonightSpread: Label every topping bowl — rookies grab faster when they can read the line.
Keep hot bases (potatoes, chips) in cambros at 200°F and cold toppings on ice if service runs long.
Put forks, napkins, and a trash can at the end of the bar — self-serve feeds get messy fast.
Build a long snack board: mains down the center, dips and chips at both ends.
Use disposable boats for handhelds so cleanup stays under five minutes after the game.
Line up Loaded Game Day Nachos on the main counter with serving spoons — firefighters grab fast between calls.
leftovers: Cool leftovers in shallow containers within two hours — deep pots stay hot too long.
Label trays with date and reheat to 165°F minimum before second shift.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Chip mountain for the whole couch. A hall pick for regular dinner nights — one line, real portions, no drama at the stove.
mealPrepNotes: Prep mise en place before the shift — Loaded Game Day Nachos runs smoother when proteins are trimmed, spices are pre-measured, and hotel pans are labeled before the first tone.
